comment: Byte budgets for what every conversation pays for when it loads the connector (improvement list M2). tools/list is sent once per conversation; diagram_capabilities and worksheet_capabilities are read before a family's first use. tools/list and per-tool sizes are UTF-8 bytes of the JSON a client receives; capabilities sizes are UTF-8 bytes of the result text a model reads (an error result fails the test). Measured 14 Nov 2026 on main 946e205: tools/list 72,220 bytes (create_worksheet 29,530, create_booklet 20,125); longest description create_booklet, 3,867 characters; capabilities text graph 58,016, bar-model 44,336, triangle 34,494, construction 27,591, cuboids 17,118, number-line 16,154, probability-tree 12,405, every other family under 12,000; worksheet_capabilities 4,812. Graph grew from 39,413 on 657aee1 with shaded inequality regions (#275), gradient triangles (#264) and house-style lines (#307); most of that is the operations schema repeating object shapes, a candidate for trimming. Each budget has about 5% headroom. Lower a budget when a change makes the catalogue smaller; raising one needs a reason in this comment and in the pull request. The family list (diagram_capabilities with no kind) gained topics and notDrawn for M89: 4,698 bytes on 14 Nov 2026. M1/M14 (15 Nov 2026, main 0ce7af7): each family's specSchema and operationsSchema now writes a shape it reuses once, in its own $defs (only when that is smaller); capabilities text graph 58,016 to 25,653, bar-model 25,894 (44,336 before v3 only) to 20,616, cuboids 17,118 to 10,879, triangle 34,494 to 32,663, construction 27,591 to 26,780, number-line 16,154 to 15,675. Budgets lowered to about 5% headroom; cuboids now uses the default. Charts raised from the default to 17,900 on 15 Nov 2026: pie charts, pictograms and scatter graphs became chart kinds (S-2, S-3, S-5), scatter with its own points, axes and line-of-best-fit schema; measured 17,055 bytes after M1/M14. Raised to 19,000 on 15 Nov 2026 for the scatter table of values and broken axes (Tim asked for both for exam coverage): measured 18,141 bytes. M10 (15 Nov 2026): every top-level spec field has a one-line description; bar-model capabilities 21,995, so its budget rises 21,600 to 23,100 (about 5% headroom). Raised list to 5,300 on 15 Nov 2026 for the angles family (its summary and topics, about 400 bytes) and to 5,900 for the area family (about 400 bytes; measured 5,706); every family adds a line here. Raised on 15 Nov 2026 for beside (two items in one card row, Tim's A7.04 marking): every leaf item gains an optional beside flag, in card and part items of both tools; measured tools/list 78,250, create_worksheet 31,941, create_booklet 21,383, so tools/list 82,200, create_worksheet 33,500 and create_booklet 22,500 (about 5% headroom). The flag carries no description of its own; the tool descriptions explain it once. Raised list 15 Nov 2026 for two more families, factor trees (N-5) and sample space diagrams (P-3): each adds a summary and topics, 6,451 bytes. Graph raised 26,900 to 32,400 on 16 Nov 2026 for transformations and vectors (worked solutions for every paper need them, Tim 16 Nov 11:57): an image object with its translate/reflect/rotate/enlarge transformation and a vector arrow on segments, in both the spec and the operations schemas; descriptions trimmed first; measured 30,861 bytes. Raised to 35,400 the same day for real-life and travel graphs (120 parts): curve objects through points (straight pieces or smooth), reading lines to the axes and an axis letter such as t; measured 33,724 bytes after trimming. Raised to 39,000 the same day for curve working (148 parts): circle objects (x² + y² = r²), tangent segments touching a curve and trapezium strips under it; measured 37,159 bytes. Raised to 43,200 the same day for equation curves in the Graph tool (quadratic, cubic, k/x, exponential and trig graphs in degrees), so tangents, strips, lines and readings apply to them for graphical solving, gradients, areas and graph transformations; measured 41,132 bytes. Charts raised to 24,600 on 16 Nov 2026: histograms, frequency polygons and cumulative frequency graphs became chart kinds sharing one grouped table (classes, a true-size graph-paper axis per kind, tables and cumulative frequency readings), needed for 192 exam parts' worked solutions; measured 23,465 bytes, with the axis patch shape written once. Raised list 6,800 to 7,400 on 16 Nov 2026 for function machines (A1.02-A1.05) and, next, written methods (NP2): measured 6,809 with function machines; each family adds about 350 bytes. Nets of 3D shapes (GM2.07, 16 Nov 2026) landed alongside written methods and box plots; nets' summary and topics were trimmed to about 250 bytes first. Raised to 27,400 on 16 Nov 2026: box plots became a chart kind (up to three plots with five hideable values each on a true-size scale, needed for the box plot exam parts' worked solutions); measured 26,050 bytes, the row and scale shapes already shared through $defs. Raised to 29,600 on 16 Nov 2026: stem-and-leaf diagrams became a chart kind (rows of a stem and its leaves with separate hide flags, a key that can be printed, left empty for pupils or left out, and the leaves column width), needed for 19 exam parts' worked solutions; measured 28,231 bytes. Raised list 7,400 to 7,800 on 16 Nov 2026 when box plots and stem-and-leaf diagrams (#404) met function machines and written methods on main: the chart topics and the two new families together measured 7,444 bytes. Charts raised to 31,900 on 16 Nov 2026: time series graphs became a chart kind (up to 24 equally spaced times, each with a label, an optional group such as a year and a hideable value, joined with straight lines on true-size graph paper), needed for the Year 10 SP8 worksheets before Christmas (Tim 16 Nov 15:41); measured 30,379 bytes, the axis shape already shared through $defs. Raised on 16 Nov 2026 for spinners, dice and bags (the probability-objects family, needed for the SP3 and SP7 worksheets before Christmas): list 7,800 to 8,500 (measured 8,096 with nets and written methods on main) and create_worksheet 33,500 to 35,300 (measured 33,586; the worksheet diagram kinds gain one family); the server instructions were trimmed to stay under 2,000 characters.
